articles.title: Node.js AI-Generated Images: 3 Rules to Compress and Upload to Cloud Storage Explained
articles.excerpt: Short answer: compress an AI-generated image before it crosses the storage boundary, upload it under a private, stable object key, and issue an expiring download link only after authorization. For a f…
articles.body: Short answer: compress an AI-generated image before it crosses the storage boundary, upload it under a private, stable object key, and issue an expiring download link only after authorization. For a fintech app handling private user uploads, the important choice is not which provider has the nicest upload snippet. It is where your application stops trusting the provider and starts enforcing tenant access. A single HTTP surface can make that handoff easier, but it cannot replace your authorization database or your recovery policy. What should the upload boundary protect? A useful flow has four distinct steps: the image is generated, Node.js transforms it, a private object is written, and an authorized request receives a temporary link. Compression belongs before the write.

articles.title: Building Delve: Making Language Practice Feel Like an Adventure
articles.excerpt: Learning a language takes more than memorising vocabulary. You need opportunities to use what you learn: to read, listen, respond, make mistakes, and try again. But practising can feel intimidating or…
articles.body: Learning a language takes more than memorising vocabulary. You need opportunities to use what you learn: to read, listen, respond, make mistakes, and try again. But practising can feel intimidating or repetitive, especially when it’s reduced to drills and flashcards. That idea was at the heart of Delve , an AI-powered language-learning game I worked on during my internship at HNG. Delve brings language practice into an interactive world where players explore different environments, complete quests, and speak with 3D characters. The goal was to make learning feel less like completing a lesson and more like taking part in an experience.## Why make language learning a game? Games give people a reason to keep going. A quest creates a goal. A new location encourages exploration.

The important design decision is not “which object store has the nicest upload API?” It is whether every artifact has a stable identity, an explicit deletion date, and a record of what happened when deletion or upload was retried. Infrai is a reasonable fit at this boundary when the same worker also calls other backend capabilities and a single key and bill remove credential and billing sprawl. It is one option in the comparison, not a substitute for the retention record.

articles.title: Where the keys go: signing on a blockchain when your users aren't crypto users
articles.excerpt: I'm Pratyush Shivam, CTO of Konfidio in Berlin, where I lead the technology behind TrustedTrucks. The photo is from Delhi in September 2026, at a business event for TrustedTrucks. I wrote my first pro…
articles.body: I'm Pratyush Shivam, CTO of Konfidio in Berlin, where I lead the technology behind TrustedTrucks. The photo is from Delhi in September 2026, at a business event for TrustedTrucks. I wrote my first production code in 2016, and a lot of my job is still deciding where the hard parts of a system should live. This post is about one of those decisions: where the keys go when ordinary business users act on a blockchain. The problem TrustedTrucks fingerprints shipment documents on a permissioned blockchain, so every company on a shipment can check which version was approved, when, and by whom. Every approval ends up as a signed entry. Signed by what, though? The people approving are dispatchers, drivers and finance teams.

articles.title: Parallel Coding Agents Without Repository Collisions
articles.excerpt: Three coding agents can finish three tasks at once. They can also overwrite the same file, reuse one port, or merge against old code. Speed only helps when each agent has a clear place to work and a s…
articles.body: Three coding agents can finish three tasks at once. They can also overwrite the same file, reuse one port, or merge against old code. Speed only helps when each agent has a clear place to work and a safe path back to the main branch. The goal is not “more agents.” The goal is useful work that can merge with less waiting and less repair. Give every agent an isolated workspace A branch is not enough when several processes use the same folder. One agent may change files while another is testing them. Build output, lock files, caches, and local databases can also collide. Use one Git worktree per coding agent. A worktree gives each agent its own folder and branch while sharing the same Git history.

For a media contact form, start by sizing that last term. Under an illustrative design budget of 10,000 submissions a day, a 12,000-byte retained submission occupies 3,600,000,000 bytes over 30 days; a 600-byte routing receipt occupies 180,000,000 bytes over the same period. These are calculated payload volumes before replicas, indexes, and backups, not observed traffic or provider charges. The full submission dominates this particular retention budget by a factor of 20. That does not establish which term dominates the whole invoice.

I am sceptical of building that thin interface as a standalone consumer business. But the engineering response is not to give up. It is to test where the system actually improves a customer's outcome. The examples below are a proposed evaluation design, not results from a product we have built or tested. Start with an outcome, not a better-looking chat Choose a narrow shopping job. For example: find shoes in the right size, within the delivered budget, with an acceptable return policy and delivery to a particular PIN code.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026.
